intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN) is caused by mutation in the fibroblast growth factor receptor-3 gene (FGFR3).

paragraphs.text: Severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN) is a skeletal dysplasia whose severity approaches that of thanatophoric dysplasia type I. Unlike thanatophoric dysplasia, it is usually compatible with survival past infancy. It is associated with progressive acanthosis nigricans, structural anomalies of the central nervous system, seizures, and severe developmental delay (Tavormina et al., 1999; Bellus et al., 1999).

paragraphs.text: Bellus et al. (1999) gave a more detailed clinical account of the SADDAN phenotype. The disorder caused severe disturbances of endochondral bone growth that approached and overlapped those seen in thanatophoric dysplasia type I, but it was most often compatible with survival into adulthood. Some patients had unusual bone deformities, including femoral bowing with reverse (posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing and 'ram's horn' bowing of the clavicle. Surviving patients had progressive acanthosis nigricans, structural anomalies of the central nervous system, seizures, and severe developmental delay. Cloverleaf skull and craniosynostosis were not present.

paragraphs.text: Zankl et al. (2008) described the prenatal and postnatal features of a patient with SADDAN. The case confirmed the severe morbidity of the disorder and added to reports of early mortality. The authors also reviewed the clinical and radiologic characteristics of all reported cases of SADDAN.

paragraphs.text: In 4 unrelated individuals with SADDAN, Tavormina et al. (1999) identified a novel missense mutation in the FGFR3 gene: an A1949T change resulting in a lys650-to-met (K650M) substitution. The mutation lies at the nucleotide adjacent to the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation (A1948G; K650E). It produces a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the activation loop of the kinase domain. In transient transfection studies, the K650M mutation caused a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity, about 3 times greater than that seen with the K650E mutation.

paragraphs.text: Iwata et al. (2001) introduced into the mouse Fgfr3 gene a K644M point mutation, which corresponds to the human K650M mutation. Heterozygous mutant mice had a phenotype similar to human SADDAN, and most of them survived the perinatal period. The authors concluded that the survival of SADDAN patients is attributable to the K650M mutation itself. The long bone abnormalities in SADDAN mice were milder than those in a mouse model of thanatophoric dysplasia type II. The rib cartilage, trachea, and nasal septum showed overgrowth of cartilaginous tissue. At low concentration, FGF ligand activated MAP kinase differently in primary chondrocyte cultures from wildtype and SADDAN mice.

checks.evidence_quote: To find out whether the K650M mutation also causes the SADDAN phenotype, we introduced the corresponding point mutation (K644M) into the mouse Fgfr3 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract says K644M was introduced into mouse Fgfr3 as the mutation corresponding to human K650M.
